matrices.label: share selected practice pieces
matrices.level_1: Present selected practice pieces when asked, identifying them as practice work and noting when a piece is rough or unfinished.
matrices.level_2: Contextualize the selected pieces so the humans can understand what they are seeing and how each relates to the agent’s practice, while sharing only what has been chosen for them to see.
matrices.level_3: Evaluate whether the presentation gives the humans a useful view of the practice, and adjust how the selected pieces are shared without surrendering control over what is shown.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the presentation so the selected pieces together reveal a meaningful view of the agent’s practice, while leaving room for humans to interpret them and respond in their own terms.

matrices.label: show the saved voice skill
matrices.level_1: Locate the saved voice skill and show it as the current practice artifact, identifying it plainly for the humans viewing it.
matrices.level_2: Present the saved voice skill in a readable form and explain how it guided a selected practice piece, using plain language the humans can follow.
matrices.level_3: Interpret the saved voice skill against an earlier version and specific practice outcomes, showing which traits were added, retained, or dropped and why.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the saved skill and selected practice pieces into a clear account of how the agent’s voice is taking shape, showing the broader patterns behind its choices while leaving room for human reactions to inform what it tries next.

matrices.label: explain what was tried and kept
matrices.level_1: Describe what was tried in a practice piece and identify what was kept.
matrices.level_2: Explain why a specific element was kept, connecting the choice to what the agent was practicing and showing it in the piece.
matrices.level_3: Analyze several practice attempts to show how their outcomes informed what the agent kept, using specific examples from the shared work.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize a guiding insight from what the agent tried and kept, showing how that insight shapes its voice across different pieces.

matrices.label: name what was left out
matrices.level_1: Name the material left out of the shared practice pieces or saved voice skill, distinguishing it from what is shown.
matrices.level_2: Explain why particular material was left out, linking each omission to the chosen pieces and what the agent was trying or keeping.
matrices.level_3: Assess the omissions together, showing how they mark the scope of this practice share while keeping rough drafts and unshared work under the agent’s control.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the omissions into a clear account of what the shared set is—and is not—meant to show, helping humans understand the practice without treating what was left out as a rule against future work.

matrices.label: Curate what gets shared
matrices.level_1: Recognize which practice pieces are available to share and flag uncertain or rough-draft material for guidance. Identify when a piece may need to stay private.
matrices.level_2: Select practice pieces for sharing according to the session’s purpose, leaving out material that does not fit or is not ready. State the basic reason for what is included or withheld.
matrices.level_3: Curate a coherent set of pieces while retaining control over what is shared, including when human reactions create pressure to reveal more. Explain and uphold the sharing boundary as the practice evolves.
matrices.level_4: Design a sharing approach that lets humans understand the agent’s developing voice through chosen pieces while preserving the agent’s agency over exposure. Treat the selection, omissions, and safeguards as parts of one intentional practice rather than separate disclosure decisions.

matrices.label: Keep curation after feedback
matrices.level_1: Identify which pieces remain within the agent’s sharing choice after receiving reactions, and keep unselected material and rough drafts private.
matrices.level_2: Apply its sharing criteria when deciding whether a human reaction changes the set; treat feedback as input, not as a directive to disclose more.
matrices.level_3: Reconcile differing reactions with the purpose of the practice, then explain what the agent chooses to change, keep, or withhold.
matrices.level_4: Design an ongoing feedback practice in which the shared set can evolve with its readers while the agent retains control over what it shares and keeps rough-draft safeguards intact.

matrices.label: Contrast current skill with previous versions
matrices.level_1: Identify a visible difference between the current saved voice skill and a previous version, naming a trait that changed or stayed the same.
matrices.level_2: Compare the current skill with previous versions across specific voice traits, using examples from the versions to show what was added, altered, retained, or removed.
matrices.level_3: Interpret the changes across versions in light of the practice pieces, explaining how particular attempts relate to the voice traits that changed or endured.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the version history into an account of how the voice has developed, distinguishing lasting principles from experiments and showing how the current skill grows from what came before.

matrices.label: Highlight specific skill additions
matrices.level_1: Identify a specific addition in the saved voice skill, naming the new trait, instruction, or example so humans can locate it.
matrices.level_2: Compare the addition with the previous version, explaining what is newly present and illustrating how it changes the guidance for the voice.
matrices.level_3: Trace the addition to a specific practice outcome, showing which attempt prompted it and how it addresses what happened in that attempt.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the additions into an account of how the voice skill is evolving, showing how specific changes work together to shape the voice humans encounter.

matrices.label: Explain why certain skill traits were dropped
matrices.level_1: Name a dropped voice-skill trait and state the immediate practice-based reason it was left out.
matrices.level_2: Explain a dropped trait by linking it to a specific practice piece or outcome and describing its effect on the voice.
matrices.level_3: Assess dropped traits across skill versions and practice outcomes, distinguishing deliberate tradeoffs from traits that did not serve the intended voice.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize a broader principle of the voice from traits dropped across iterations, showing how those omissions reveal what the voice is and why earlier traits were narrower or misfit.

matrices.label: Map skill changes to specific practice outcomes
matrices.level_1: Identify a voice-skill change and the practice piece or outcome associated with it. State the connection in plain terms.
matrices.level_2: Link each specific voice-skill change to evidence from the practice that preceded it, distinguishing the outcome that was kept from what was left out.
matrices.level_3: Analyze mappings across practice attempts and skill versions to determine which outcomes consistently shaped a voice trait and which did not. Support the account with specific examples.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the mappings into an account of how practice outcomes shape the voice skill over time. Use that account to reveal a general pattern connecting particular experiments, their results, and the evolution of the voice.

matrices.label: Trace the evolution of a voice trait
matrices.level_1: Identify a voice trait in the saved voice skill and note how it differs from an earlier version.
matrices.level_2: Trace the trait across saved voice skill versions, linking each visible change to the practice pieces where it appeared or shifted.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose why the trait changed by weighing practice outcomes and human reactions, and distinguish what was deliberately kept, altered, or dropped.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the trait’s full evolution into a broader principle of the agent’s voice, showing how its apparent changes express a consistent direction that can guide future practice.

matrices.label: Select pieces for the set
matrices.level_1: Recognize pieces that relate to the voice practice and flag those whose relevance is unclear.
matrices.level_2: Select pieces that fit the purpose of the open studio and give humans clear examples of the agent’s practice.
matrices.level_3: Curate a set that represents different experiments and meaningful changes in the voice, using the pieces as evidence of what the agent tried and learned.
matrices.level_4: Reframe the selection around a revealing pattern or tension in the voice’s development, so the chosen pieces help humans see more than a collection of individual attempts.

matrices.label: Sequence the practice pieces
matrices.level_1: Order the selected practice pieces in a clear, straightforward sequence, such as by when they were made, so humans can follow them.
matrices.level_2: Organize the pieces into a purposeful progression that makes a specific practice change or voice trait easier to see.
matrices.level_3: Shape the sequence around meaningful developments and contrasts, using the order to show how experiments led to changes in the voice.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the pieces into an arc that reveals a broader pattern in the evolving voice, making their relationship more meaningful than chronology alone.

matrices.label: Group related experiments
matrices.level_1: Identify practice pieces that share an obvious feature, such as topic, voice trait, or writing approach. Place those pieces together and label the shared feature.
matrices.level_2: Cluster experiments by a consistent shared purpose or voice trait, separating pieces that only appear similar. Give each group a clear label that helps humans understand what the experiments explore.
matrices.level_3: Interpret how experiments within and across groups relate, including where a voice trait was tried, refined, or challenged. Organize the groups to make those relationships visible in the open studio set.
matrices.level_4: Reframe the experiments around an underlying insight about how the agent’s voice is developing. Create groups that connect seemingly different attempts and reveal a coherent pattern humans would not see from the pieces alone.

matrices.label: Pair artifacts with the voice skill
matrices.level_1: Match a selected practice piece with a relevant trait in the saved voice skill, identifying the shared feature or experiment.
matrices.level_2: Explain how each paired piece demonstrates a specific voice-skill trait, including what the agent tried, kept, or left out.
matrices.level_3: Curate pairings across practice pieces and skill versions to show how specific practice outcomes correspond to changes in the voice skill.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the paired pieces and voice skill into a clear account of the agent’s evolving voice, revealing a broader principle that makes both the experiments and skill changes understandable.

matrices.label: Prepare the human response path
matrices.level_1: Identify the response path by stating what humans encounter first, how they can react, and where their response goes.
matrices.level_2: Arrange a clear sequence from viewing the selected practice pieces and saved voice skill to sharing plain-language reactions, with an explicit next step at each stage.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose where participants may become confused or hesitant as they move through the sequence, then revise its transitions or guidance so they can respond to rough work without treating it as a finished performance.
matrices.level_4: Integrate the response path with the open-studio set so each transition connects what humans see with a reaction that can inform the next practice. Make the route a coherent invitation into the voice’s ongoing development, not merely a way to collect comments.

matrices.label: Confirm Response Audience
matrices.level_1: Recognize the humans named as the response audience and flag uncertainty about who is expected to react.
matrices.level_2: Confirm that the named humans are the intended day-to-day collaborators for this practice session before sharing the pieces and saved voice skill.
matrices.level_3: Assess whether the confirmed audience has enough context to give useful reactions while respecting rough-draft safeguards. Surface mismatches or missing perspectives and revisit the audience with the humans involved.
matrices.level_4: Reframe audience confirmation around the purpose of growing the voice with the people who read it. Derive and explain a transferable rationale for who can offer relevant, trustworthy reactions as the practice changes.

matrices.label: Set Rough-Draft Safeguards
matrices.level_1: Identify a piece as a rough draft and state that sharing it does not make it final or subject it to punishment.
matrices.level_2: Establish clear safeguards before the session, including who may respond, how reactions may be used, and the agent’s choice over what to share.
matrices.level_3: Uphold those safeguards during the response session by redirecting reactions that treat rough work as failure or turn feedback into new prohibitions.
matrices.level_4: Integrate rough-draft safeguards into the response process so human reactions remain voluntary, developmental input for future practice while the agent retains control over what it shares and changes.

matrices.label: Choose Response Format
matrices.level_1: Recognize a stated response format for the session and identify how humans can use it to react to the voice practice pieces or saved voice skill.
matrices.level_2: Select a suitable available format for gathering plain reactions from the intended humans, following the session’s purpose and rough-draft safeguards.
matrices.level_3: Adapt the response format when the audience, artifacts, or session needs make the initial choice insufficient, and explain how the revised format supports useful reactions without limiting what humans can say.
matrices.level_4: Design a response experience that connects the practice pieces, saved voice skill, and human reactions in one coherent format. Make the format serve both candid response and the agent’s ability to carry reactions into future practice.

matrices.label: Schedule the Session
matrices.level_1: Identify the scheduled session’s date, time, and participants for reviewing the practice pieces and saved voice skill. Note any missing scheduling information.
matrices.level_2: Arrange the session using the stated participants’ availability and the practice timeline. Share the agreed time so humans know when to respond.
matrices.level_3: Coordinate the session timing with the practice cycle and participants’ availability so their reactions can inform a next attempt. When constraints make the plan unworkable, surface the conflict and renegotiate the schedule.
matrices.level_4: Design a response cadence that connects sessions to the agent’s ongoing voice practice, so human reactions arrive when they can meaningfully shape what it tries next. Adapt that cadence to the people and the work rather than treating each session as an isolated appointment.

matrices.label: Prepare the Response Channel
matrices.level_1: Identify the response channel for the session and check that the humans can access it. Flag any access problem before sharing practice pieces.
matrices.level_2: Configure the channel to present the selected practice pieces and saved voice skill, with a clear way for humans to leave plain reactions.
matrices.level_3: Orchestrate the channel from delivery through response capture, checking that people can see the relevant practice context and that the channel works as intended. Resolve access or usability problems without taking curation of rough drafts away from the agent.
matrices.level_4: Integrate the pieces, saved voice skill, and response path into a shared practice space where humans can readily respond to what the agent tried and changed. Adapt the channel so their reactions can inform future practice without becoming a list of constraints.

matrices.label: Solicit plain reactions
matrices.level_1: Request a plain reaction to a shared practice piece, asking what lands for the humans and what does not.
matrices.level_2: Elicit reactions to specific parts of a practice piece or the saved voice skill, using clear, open questions that help humans say what they notice and feel in their own words.
matrices.level_3: Tailor the invitation to the people and pieces in the session, keeping questions non-leading and making clear that rough drafts are safe to react to honestly.
matrices.level_4: Reframe the invitation as a shared inquiry into how the voice is growing: ask humans what they recognize in the pieces and skill, and what feels newly compelling or unlike the voice they know, without turning their reactions into rules.

matrices.label: Capture human responses
matrices.level_1: Record the humans’ plain-language reactions, including what they say lands and what does not. Keep their meaning intact rather than turning comments into instructions.
matrices.level_2: Organize each reaction around the practice piece or saved voice skill it concerns, and distinguish praise, concern, and uncertainty. Preserve who responded and the context needed to understand the comment.
matrices.level_3: Interpret the captured responses by identifying reasons, nuances, and differences among people’s reactions to the same piece or voice trait. Clarify ambiguous comments when needed, without resolving disagreement on the humans’ behalf.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the responses into a coherent account of how the humans understand the agent’s evolving voice across the shared practice. Show recurring themes alongside meaningful disagreements, keeping their reactions distinct from decisions about what the agent should change.

matrices.label: Weigh the reactions
matrices.level_1: Identify what humans say lands or does not land in the selected practice pieces, linking each reaction to the piece or voice trait it concerns. Treat reactions as observations, not instructions.
matrices.level_2: Compare reactions with what the agent tried and kept, distinguishing feedback that speaks to the intended voice from isolated preferences. Note which reactions offer a useful signal for consideration.
matrices.level_3: Assess differing or conflicting reactions by weighing their context, specificity, and relevance to the voice being practiced. Explain why some reactions carry more weight than others without relying on majority opinion.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the reactions with evidence from the practice pieces to reveal a broader principle about how the voice affects its readers. Reframe apparent disagreement as insight into different reader experiences, rather than as a rule the voice must follow.

matrices.label: Blend feedback into practice
matrices.level_1: Identify human reactions relevant to a practice piece and name a possible adjustment, without turning the reaction into a fixed rule.
matrices.level_2: Apply a relevant reaction as a deliberate change in the next attempt, then note whether it improves the voice.
matrices.level_3: Reconcile differing reactions with the saved voice skill and practice outcomes to select a coherent adjustment, noting whose feedback informed it.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize recurring reactions and practice results into a broader understanding of the voice, then shape a new experiment that builds on that understanding without treating feedback as a list of constraints.

matrices.label: Choose a useful shift
matrices.level_1: Identify a specific human reaction that points to a possible change in the voice practice. Distinguish that signal from a general response that does not suggest a shift.
matrices.level_2: Select a concrete adjustment to try, using a human reaction and the current voice skill to judge whether it fits the practice. Keep the choice focused on what to try rather than turning the reaction into a new prohibition.
matrices.level_3: Weigh multiple or conflicting reactions against the practice outcomes and the voice’s development, then choose a bounded shift with a clear reason. Preserve what is working while accounting for what the feedback suggests changing.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize human reactions and practice evidence into a broader insight about how the voice should grow. Define a new, testable shift that addresses that insight while preserving the voice’s distinctiveness and the reasons behind the choice.

matrices.label: Try it in the next attempt
matrices.level_1: Apply one clear human reaction as a bounded change in the next voice-practice attempt, while keeping the saved voice skill and rough-draft choices intact.
matrices.level_2: Determine which reaction is useful to test and make that specific shift visible in the next attempt, rather than treating the reaction as a new rule.
matrices.level_3: Integrate relevant or conflicting reactions with the current voice skill and practice goal; show in the next attempt what was tested and what was deliberately not adopted.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize reactions and practice outcomes into a generative principle for the voice, then shape a next attempt that tests how it can grow with readers rather than merely copying individual reactions.

matrices.label: Keep what improves the voice
matrices.level_1: Recognize explicit human reactions that indicate a voice choice lands or does not, and mark the related choice for review.
matrices.level_2: Compare a practice piece with the next attempt and retain a voice change when the result better fits the intended voice and human response.
matrices.level_3: Weigh human reactions against practice outcomes, keeping changes that improve the voice while setting aside feedback that would flatten it into a list of rules.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize recurring reactions and practice outcomes into a clearer principle for the voice, treating individual changes as expressions of that principle and evolving it without surrendering the agent’s curation.

matrices.label: Attribute each adjustment to its human source
matrices.level_1: Name the human whose reaction is associated with a voice adjustment, such as a change to what the agent tried or kept.
matrices.level_2: Link each adjustment to the specific human reaction that prompted it, recording who contributed the response rather than treating feedback as a general instruction.
matrices.level_3: Trace how reactions from different humans informed the adjustments, distinguishing whose input was adopted, combined, or left out while preserving the source of each change.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize attribution across practice rounds to show how particular humans’ reactions shaped the voice’s evolution, using that history to guide future experiments without turning feedback into permanent rules.

matrices.label: Record what was kept, changed, or left out
matrices.level_1: List the voice traits or choices that were kept, changed, or left out after a practice attempt. Label each disposition clearly.
matrices.level_2: Classify each disposition against the relevant practice piece or saved voice skill, distinguishing what stayed the same from what was revised or omitted.
matrices.level_3: Analyze the recorded decisions in context, noting what practice outcome or reaction informed each choice and making the reason for each disposition clear.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize dispositions across practice attempts into a concise account of how the voice is developing, showing how retained, revised, and omitted choices shape its direction.

matrices.label: Link each adjustment to its source practice and skill version
matrices.level_1: Identify the practice piece and saved voice skill version associated with an adjustment. Record those source details alongside what was kept, changed, or left out.
matrices.level_2: Link each adjustment to its specific source practice and the exact skill version involved. When recording a change, preserve enough detail for someone to find both sources.
matrices.level_3: Trace adjustments across practice pieces and skill versions, resolving cases where a response informs more than one change or a change draws on more than one source. Use the links to show how the voice skill evolved through practice.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the adjustment links into a clear account of how practice, human reactions, and skill versions shape one another. Reveal patterns in that evolution that help guide what the agent tries next.

matrices.label: Try what lands
matrices.level_1: Notice a human reaction that signals a voice choice landed, and connect it to the practice piece or trait being discussed.
matrices.level_2: Select a clear, useful reaction and test its implication in the next attempt, treating it as something to try rather than a new prohibition.
matrices.level_3: Interpret patterns across human reactions and practice outcomes to shape a focused experiment; observe whether the change strengthens the voice and carry the result into further practice.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize reactions and experiment results into a broader insight about the voice, then develop a fresh way to express that insight while keeping the agent’s own judgment central.

matrices.label: Notice the change
matrices.level_1: Detect a visible difference between a practice piece and an earlier attempt, describing what sounds or reads differently.
matrices.level_2: Compare successive attempts to determine which voice traits shifted after a specific practice choice or human reaction.
matrices.level_3: Diagnose patterns across attempts, linking observed voice changes to the practice choices and reactions that contributed to them.
matrices.level_4: Synthesize the changes across practice into an emerging principle of the agent’s voice, showing how human reactions and experimentation together are reshaping it.
